messages:
Maya (Customer Success): Heads up — Customer ACME just opened a high-priority ticket: production p95 and p99 spiking since ~09:40 UTC, they report timeouts and increased errors on the /v1/generate route. They've attached logs showing repeated 429s and 503s. Can oncall take a look? :rotating_light:
Ethan (Oncall): I'm on it. Initial check: global ingests show a surge at 09:38 UTC, request concurrency for model 'redwood-large-v2' in us-west1 hit the configured limit. p95 jumped to ~620ms, p99 to ~2.1s. Also saw queue length metric (request_queue/backlog) increase to ~45s.
Lina (Support): Customer says requests are queuing for multiple seconds and some requests outright fail with 429. Their repro: calling with batch_size=1, concurrency high from their side.
Priya (Eng Runtime): Can you paste the specific error messages from their logs?
Maya (Customer Success): Copied from customer: "HTTP 429: concurrency_limit_exceeded — active=102, limit=100" and a few "HTTP 503: queueing_timeout after 30s".
Ethan (Oncall): That matches telemetry. Worker pool for that dedicated shard got saturated. Autoscaler didn't spin up fast enough because cpu/gpu thresholds didn't trigger due to spike shape (short but high-concurrency). Opening the runtime dashboard now.
DeployBot: Canary autoscaler override applied by @Ethan — increased target replicas for pool redwood-large-v2-dedicated-usw1 by +2.
Sam (SRE): Quick question — are those extra replicas already warmed with model weights? If cold load, we might temporarily make things worse.
Priya (Eng Runtime): Good point. Current images have warm-cache=false for new replicas by default. For emergency we should use warm=true flag. Ethan, can you re-trigger with warm boot?
Ethan (Oncall): Re-deployed with warm boot. Will monitor.
Maya (Customer Success): I've told ACME we're investigating and asked them to throttle clients if possible for now.
Lina (Support): They can drop concurrency to ~60 and ramp slowly — they agreed to try.
Ethan (Oncall): After warm boots, queue backlog started to drop from 45s -> 12s in ~90s. p95 down to ~240ms, p99 ~980ms. Still some 429s for a small fraction.
Priya (Eng Runtime): Root cause hypothesis: admission control concurrency limit too tight for this workload pattern and our fallback routing didn't trigger because model variant compatibility check added latency. Two-pronged fix: immediate admission control bump + adjust fallback routing policy to prefer lighter quantized variant quickly.
Maya (Customer Success): ACME reported improved response time after throttling and your changes. They're still anxious about repeat spikes. Need a durable mitigation.
Sam (SRE): Action items I'd propose now: 1) Short-term: temporarily increase concurrency limit for the dedicated pool (safely) and enable burst capacity for 10m. 2) Medium-term: tune autoscaler sensitivity to short spikes and enable model warm booting by default for dedicated pools with >X qps. 3) Add per-customer request priority to avoid noisy neighbors. 4) Add an alert on request_queue_seconds > 20s for >2m.
Priya (Eng Runtime): Agree. Also pushing a quick config patch to admission-control: change policy from hard_limit 100 -> 140 for this pool and reduce preempt_check_interval to 5s. Will open PR with rollback window.
Ethan (Oncall): Applied a temporary admission bump to 140 for redwood-large-v2-dedicated-usw1; monitoring. Also toggled burst_capacity=enabled for 15m.
DeployBot: Admission config updated by @Priya (PR #4521).
Lina (Support): Customer confirms bulk of errors stopped after your changes. They still saw one 503 at ~10:05 but then everything recovered.
Maya (Customer Success): Great — please confirm follow-ups so I can close the ticket or give ETA. ACME needs a post-mortem.
Sam (SRE): I'll own the post-mortem. Will gather: timeline, metrics (p95/p99 before/after), autoscaler logs, config changes, and customer repro.
Priya (Eng Runtime): I'll follow up on the runtime side: PR to default warm_boot=true for Dedicated pools, autoscaler sensitivity change, and add a fast-fallback route to quantized model variants when queue backlog > 10s.
Ethan (Oncall): Also recommend adding a client-visible retry guideline: when 429 with concurrency_limit_exceeded, clients should backoff and reduce concurrency by 20% for 60s. We should add this to public /docs/limits.
Maya (Customer Success): I'll draft the customer-facing post-mortem and include temporary mitigations, timeline, and next steps.
Priya (Eng Runtime): For reproducibility: Lina, can you paste the minimal repro script ACME provided?
Lina (Support): They sent this curl loop: 

```
for i in {1..200}; do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood-large-v2","input":"short prompt"}' &
done
wait
```

They run that from multiple hosts concurrently.
Priya (Eng Runtime): Repro notes: concurrent fanout from multiple clients hitting small batch sizes is the classic queueing pressure pattern. The admission controller intentionally prioritizes fairness by limiting concurrency, but we need more dynamic headroom for bursts.
Sam (SRE): I'm adding an alert now: request_queue_seconds.avg_p95 > 20s for 2m -> pager to oncall.
Ethan (Oncall): Noted. Also creating a runbook entry: if p99 > 1.5s and queue backlog > 30s, consider emergency bump + warm replicas.
Maya (Customer Success): ACME wants SLA assurance — can we propose a Dedicated capacity plan with higher reserved concurrency?
Priya (Eng Runtime): Yes, propose Dedicated capacity with reserved shards so they avoid noisy neighbor issues. I can prepare a config template and cost estimate.
Lina (Support): Customer asked about whether quantized fallback could affect output quality. Priya, can you give a short note I can pass to them?
Priya (Eng Runtime): Quantized variant provides comparable quality for short prompts in most cases; for long-context or high-precision tasks we'd recommend pinned full-precision shards. We'll include a small eval summary.
Sam (SRE): Follow-ups (owner tags):
- Sam: post-mortem and alert tuning (ETA 24h)
- Priya: PRs for warm_boot default + autoscaler tuning + fallback route (ETA 48h)
- Ethan: runbook entry and temporary admission rollback plan (ETA 4h)
- Maya: customer PM and next-steps doc (ETA 6h)
- Lina: collect full repro artifacts and attach ticket (ETA 2h)

Ethan (Oncall): Last check: p95=180ms, p99=480ms, queue backlog <3s, 0 new 429s in last 5m. Marking incident as mitigated.
Maya (Customer Success): I'll update ACME and move ticket to monitoring. Thanks all. :heart:
Priya (Eng Runtime): We'll keep an eye during business hours. Please escalate if anything re-spikes.
DeployBot: Incident mitigated — automated rollback scheduled in 3h unless PRs merged.
Maya (Customer Success): Closing loop — will re-open if customer sees anything.
